title: The classical Heegner hypothesis is a local test
status: Developed classical result with a scoped worked example
summary: A formal q-deformation must begin with a correctly specified classical construction. The conductor and quadratic field already decide whether the standard X0(N) Heegner-point setup applies.
definitions: Use the classical Heegner hypothesis: every rational prime dividing the conductor N splits in the imaginary quadratic field K.
For the source curve N=32. Q(i) has discriminant-4; a prime dividing the discriminant is ramified rather than split.

result.name: Failure at2 and a split-prime alternative
result.statement: The source pair fails the classical split-prime hypothesis because2 ramifies in Q(i). In Q(sqrt(-7)),2 splits, so the prime condition for level32 is satisfied.
result.proof: In Z[i],2=-i(1+i)², proving ramification directly. In the ring of integers Z[(1+sqrt(-7))/2], the generator theta satisfies theta²-theta+2=0. Modulo2 its polynomial is X(X-1), with two distinct roots. Dedekind factorization, or the corresponding two distinct norm-two ideals, therefore gives splitting of2. These calculations check the exact local premise of the classical modular-curve construction. They do not supply the height formula, prove a point has infinite order or define a q-deformation. A generalized Heegner construction allowing ramification would require its own different hypotheses.

example.setup: Compare discriminants-4 and-7 at the unique prime dividing32.
example.calculation: The first has discriminant divisible by2 and a repeated factor; the second has discriminant congruent1 modulo8 and distinct factors over F2. No numerical period calculation is required for this decision.
example.conclusion: The starting field can be chosen to meet a precise classical condition before any formal deformation is attempted.

limits: A satisfied Heegner hypothesis alone does not imply a nonzero L-derivative or a non-torsion point. Formal power-series coordinates are not automatically points on the original elliptic curve.
extension: Specify the modular parametrization and CM ideal, compute a genuine classical Heegner point, verify its curve equation, and only then formulate an algebraic deformation with a proved specialization map.

title: A calibrated search has a computable multiplicity cost
status: Developed classical result with a scoped worked example
summary: The source moonshine interpretation selected fitted coordinates and reported a significance value. A finite family of tests gives an exact mathematical benchmark for distinguishing one prespecified statistic from a selected maximum.
definitions: Let p1,...,pM be valid null p-values, so Pr(pj<=u)<=u for each j.
Define p_adj=min(1,M*min_j pj). Independence is not assumed for the familywise bound.

result.name: Finite-search familywise control
result.statement: Pr(p_adj<=alpha)<=alpha. If the p-values are independent uniform variables, Pr(min pj<=u)=1-(1-u)^M exactly.
result.proof: The event p_adj<=alpha is contained in the union of events pj<=alpha/M. The union bound gives probability at most sum_j alpha/M=alpha, proving the adjusted test. Under independence, the complementary event pj>u for all j has probability(1-u)^M, giving the exact formula. The theorem concerns the whole specified search family: fitting extra parameters, choosing observables after inspection or retaining only successful seeds enlarges that family or requires a different null calibration. A held-out evaluation can avoid reusing the same observations for both selection and confirmation.

example.setup: As a newly stipulated illustration, take M=1000 independent null tests and u=0.001.
example.calculation: The chance of at least one such small p-value is1-0.999^1000, approximately0.6323. Thus a selected value0.001 does not carry the interpretation of one prespecified test.
example.conclusion: The cost of selection can be computed without asserting any physical mechanism or interpreting fitted couplings as predictions.

limits: The exact independence formula is illustrative. The historical search size, data covariance and original analysis are unavailable, so no corrected historical significance is claimed.
extension: Freeze the observables and coordinate map, simulate the complete selection procedure under a stated correlated null, and compare a separately held-out statistic with that calibrated distribution.

title: Compounding distinguishes price growth from purchasing-power decay
status: Developed classical result with a scoped worked example
summary: The source challenged an invented annual rate. The mathematical repair is to state a hypothetical rate transparently and distinguish the two reciprocal quantities before inserting any empirical index.
definitions: Let the annual price multiplier be1+pi>0 and the annual purchasing-power multiplier be1-d>0.
Purchasing power is reciprocal to the price index for a fixed nominal amount and a fixed basket.

result.name: Exact reciprocal compounding
result.statement: (1-d)=1/(1+pi), so d=pi/(1+pi). After T years the price factor is(1+pi)^T and the purchasing-power factor is(1-d)^T.
result.proof: If one basket costs P0 initially and PT=P0(1+pi)^T later, a fixed nominal amount buys PT/P0 times fewer baskets; its relative purchasing power is P0/PT. Equating the annual reciprocal factor with1-d gives the stated conversion. For variable annual rates pi_t, replace the power by the product of(1+pi_t); averaging rates arithmetically does not in general reproduce that product. The constant equivalent annual rate is exp[T^(-1)sum log(1+pi_t)]-1. These are index identities, not estimates of any country or historical period.

example.setup: Stipulate d=0.033 for T=30; do not treat it as a measured historical rate.
example.calculation: The purchasing-power factor is0.967^30, approximately0.3654, and the reciprocal price factor is about2.7366. The corresponding price inflation rate is0.033/0.967, approximately3.4126 percent, rather than3.3 percent.
example.conclusion: The example separates a mathematical scenario from the missing empirical rate and keeps numerator and denominator conventions consistent.

limits: Actual purchasing power depends on a declared basket, index construction, time window and source series. No current inflation or investment conclusion is inferred from this hypothetical example.
extension: Given a specified historical index series, compute log growth by interval, chain the factors exactly to the available decimal precision, and quantify how alternative basket definitions change the result.
